inspiration: upstream Ghidra RuleSubRight (ruleaction.cc:7271-7340, GHIDRA_REV=cef869af); openssh-portable ssh sshbuf_put_u64 @ 0x4cd60; corpus-wide 5,919 nonzero-offset SUBPIECEs in 2,394 functions vs ghidra's 18 in 13
gating_rationale: SUBnn is an undeclared identifier, so the pre-fix output does not compile; the fix restores upstream Ghidra's own behavior from an explicitly-marked port stub rather than making a judgment call; the ablation moves 0/675 upstream assertions; and `option togglerule subright off` already gives a bisector the pre-fix rendering because `subright` is a registered rule-group name in the action pool. Recorded in docs/history.md as a Convergence (upstream behavior restored), not a DIV row.

residual_classification.note: every residual is a case upstream's own guards decline: the addr-tied/overlap==c ActionCopyMarker bail (89) and the isPieceStructured special-print branch (6). The global-array family is round 1's separately-filed `rodata-phantom-store`; the local family is the P6 partial-symbol thread that renders `sym._2_2_` upstream. subright owns 1,817 of the 1,912 (95.0%).

breadth.measured_cost: exactly two functions in 14,720 gain a dead partial-register shift statement -- `(undefined7)((uint8)a2 >> 8)` in bzip2 sub_da00 and one `(undefined3)((uint4)v11 >> 8)` on ARM. That is the SUB87/SUB43 form, which upstream lowers the same way. Corpus-wide count of that shape: 0 -> 2.

decisions.question: Should the restored RuleSubRight tail ship behind a named --option, or ungated?
decisions.decider: independent subagent, given CLAUDE.md's feature/bug-fix rule, improvement-pipeline standing requirement 3, the precedent commits, and docs/options.md
decisions.verbatim: VERDICT: ungated. CLAUDE.md's rule gates *features* -- 'behavior that is a judgment call, not universally better' -- and exempts 'a strict bug fix that only corrects wrong output.' SUB81 is an undeclared identifier, so the old output is not C; the new form is byte-identical in shape to upstream Ghidra's, which is the port's fidelity target. There is no honest `use_when` to write: no user ever wants the non-compiling spelling, and options.md's prose format demands a real 'flip it when...' case. Precedent is unanimous for exactly this shape. b0752b83 (DIV-49) is the closest analogue -- an unported upstream call (BlockGraph::orderBlocks) restored, blast radius 0.87% of functions, commit body: 'Strict bug fix restoring upstream behavior -- no option (the current output is unambiguously wrong C).' 694ab8ef/DIV-46 uses the identical 'neither PTRSUB nor ESP is declared anywhere, so the function is not C' reasoning; 36641d35/DIV-50 ('No option: the affected functions produced no output at all before'), 41c26929/DIV-48 and 36fe8d90/DIV-52 all change emitted C ungated. None of the five touches phases.toml, options.rs, or a catalog count. [Required artifacts:] docs/history.md row (Convergences table -- a fix that moves kuna back onto upstream's default earns no DIV row); spec prose in docs/spec/03-ssa-and-simplification.md; tests/stages/<slug>.xml two-pass end-to-end testcase -- pass 2 can pin the bug form with the existing `option togglerule subright off`, satisfying the two-pass convention with no new flag; tests/stages/README.md line, corpus file count in kuna-base/src/xml.rs, re-recorded docs/baseline-stages.json; commit body carrying corpus breadth and speed deltas. [Strongest counter, and why it loses:] The one Convergence row on the books, callsitestackargs, *did* add a default-ON option whose `off` 'reproduces the pre-fix output for bisection' -- and 3.1% of functions is a wider blast radius than any ungated precedent (0.87% for DIV-49). But that option existed to buy a bisection switch for an inline predicate inside check_input_trial_use with no rule-group name. Here the switch already exists: subright is a registered rule group (universalaction.rs:552) reachable via togglerule. The only thing a new settableTable row would add is catalog-count churn and a documented knob nobody should ever flip.

decisions.question: Where does the new logic live -- a new kuna_subright.rs module, or in place?
decisions.rationale: The kuna_<slug>.rs convention is for NEW logic that is a judgment call. This is the completion of a ported rule that already exists in its 1:1-anchored port file (`ruleaction.cc:7271 / ruleaction.hh:1165`), is already registered in the cleanup pool, and already carries the first half of its own body. Splitting the tail into a separate module would break the file's port anchoring for no gain.
